nodes.label: Shape and color hint at what kind of sign it is

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: The overview fact says shape and color hint at a sign's kind, while the rectangle fact shows one shape serving regulatory, guide, and warning signs; learners expect every shape to mean one thing.

nodes.label: Red means stop, yield, or obey the sign

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Red means stop, yield, or obey, and the contrast fact adds that red commands an action while white states the enforceable rule behind such commands; learners swap the command color with the rule color.

nodes.label: Green gives direction and distance to a place

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Green gives direction, and the contrast fact lines up green for the way, blue for services and brown for recreation; learners mix up which guide color does which.

nodes.label: Blue points travelers to services

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Blue points to services such as fuel and lodging, while brown guides to recreation and cultural points of interest such as parks and historic sites; both are destination colors that learners swap.

nodes.label: Brown guides to recreation and cultural sites

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Blue points to services such as fuel and lodging, while brown guides to recreation and cultural points of interest such as parks and historic sites; both are destination colors that learners swap.
Brown guides to recreation and cultural sites, and the contrast fact separates it from green for the way and blue for services; learners expect brown to cover services too.

nodes.label: A yellow traffic sign gives a general warning.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Yellow signals a general warning, and the contrast fact reserves fluorescent yellow-green for pedestrian, bicycle, and school warnings; learners treat the two yellows as one.

nodes.label: Fluorescent yellow-green marks pedestrian, bicycle and school warnings

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Fluorescent yellow-green marks pedestrian, bicycle, and school warnings, while the contrast fact keeps plain yellow for general hazards; learners mix the two shades.

nodes.label: White carries regulatory messages about enforceable laws

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: White carries regulatory messages, and the contrast fact says red commands an action while white states the enforceable rule; learners assume only red signs carry laws.

nodes.label: Orange warns of road work and temporary traffic control

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Orange warns of road work and temporary traffic control, and the contrast fact separates it from yellow, which marks general warnings with no work-zone tie; learners treat orange as just another warning color.

nodes.label: Fluorescent pink marks incident-management warnings

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: Fluorescent pink marks incident-management warnings, and the contrast fact says pink covers incident response such as crash cleanup while orange covers road work and maintenance; learners merge the two temporary colors.

nodes.label: The octagon belongs to the stop sign alone and demands a full stop

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: The octagon belongs to the stop sign and demands a full stop, and the contrast fact adds that the triangle asks only a yield although both control intersections; learners blur the two intersection shapes.

nodes.label: The triangle-shaped sign means yield the right of way

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: The triangle means yield the right of way, and the contrast fact says the octagon demands a full stop while the triangle asks only a yield; learners upgrade the yield to a stop.

nodes.label: Rectangles serve as regulatory, guide and warning signs

nodes.label: The pennant on the left warns passing is prohibited ahead

nodes.label: The diamond warns of special road hazards

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: start with the rule that shape and color hint at a sign's kind, then teach red, white, green, blue, brown, yellow and yellow-green one color at a time, closing with the two color contrasts
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: one-fact cards per color plus the red-versus-white and green-blue-brown contrast cards
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: module quiz on which color carries which kind of message

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: teach orange for road work and fluorescent pink for incident response, then contrast each against plain yellow and each other
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: one-fact cards on orange and pink plus the three color-contrast cards
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: module quiz on which color marks road work, incidents and general hazards

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: teach the octagon and the triangle as the two intersection-control shapes, then the rectangle's three jobs, closing with the stop-versus-yield contrast
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: one-fact cards on the octagon, the triangle, the rectangle and the octagon-versus-triangle contrast
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: module quiz on which shape demands a stop, which asks a yield and what rectangles carry

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: teach the no-passing pennant, the hazard diamond, the railroad circle, the school pentagon and the crossbuck with its track-count plate, then the three shape contrasts
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: one-fact cards per shape plus the circle-versus-crossbuck, pennant-versus-diamond and rectangle-versus-diamond contrasts
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: module quiz on which shape marks no passing, hazards, railroads and schools
